answer: In an agent economy%2C Sybil resistance arises when each identity must continuously operate a unique ferrous hardware enclave generating non-transferable attestation proofs. These bind the agent to physical silicon traits that cannot be replicated cheaply. An attacker spawning many fakes faces the cost of fabricating separate enclaves for every identity and sustaining the compute load needed to bridge the canyon of latency and verification rounds. The velvet smoothness of legitimate long-term participation is rewarded%2C while short-lived clones are filtered by rising energy costs.
